issues.legal_issue: A statutory prohibition on passing decrees in pre-emption suits applies when an appeal from a trial-court decree remains pending after the prohibition takes effect, because the appeal reopens the subject matter and the appellate decree replaces the trial decree.
material_facts: A trial court had passed a decree enforcing a right of pre-emption.
After the statutory prohibition on passing decrees in pre-emption suits took effect, the decree was challenged in appellate proceedings and the dispute remained pending on further appeal.
The appellate hearing reopened the subject matter of the trial decree.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition applies to the appellate decree as well as to a decree at trial. The appeal was allowed and the pre-emption suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Punjab Pre-emption (Repeal) Act, 1973 bars a court from passing a decree in a pre-emption suit from the Act's commencement. An appeal is a rehearing of the whole subject matter, and the trial decree merges into the appellate decree, so the statutory bar applies to a decree passed in appeal. The Court relied on Official Liquidator v. R. Desikachar.

rule.if: preemption_suit_appeal and trial_decree_under_review and decree_bar_became_effective and appellate_hearing_reopens_subject_matter

predicates.preemption_suit_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a suit seeking enforcement of a right of pre-emption.
predicates.trial_decree_under_review: A trial court has passed a decree in the suit, and that decree is under review in the appeal.
predicates.decree_bar_became_effective: A statutory prohibition on passing decrees in such suits took effect before the appellate court passes its decree.
predicates.appellate_hearing_reopens_subject_matter: The appellate hearing reopens the whole subject matter of the trial decree.

issues.definition: When an appeal reopens a trial decree in a pre-emption suit after a statutory bar on decrees in such suits has taken effect, the suit is dismissed.
